next_three_research_scopes.title: Chunk-size choices for causal long prefill under GPU memory limits
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: For long causal or recurrent GPU prefill, compare smaller, current-size and larger chunks, including how to treat a short tail. Which workload and device conditions justify each choice when GEMM/tile utilization, launch amortization, live workspace, memory traffic and shared-state dependencies all matter?
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use current SYCL/Intel primary documentation and original non-LLM GPU/ASIC papers or engineering blogs. Compare at least three chunk-size strategies and a tail strategy; include evidence where a smaller chunk reduces live memory but loses throughput to launch or tile underfill, and where a larger chunk worsens residency or memory pressure. Keep design estimates separate from measured results. Do not repeat R769's buffer/queue-overlap comparison, R667's execution-order audit, or claim B570 performance.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,800 words; at most 7 substantive primary sources, exact links, applicability limits and a counterevidence table.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisites: Long-prefill chunk tuning remains in scope; this is bounded knowledge collection and does not require a new local measurement before research.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: AGENTS.md keeps long-prefill chunk-size tuning active; R769 compares fixed 8,192-row buffers but does not compare chunk sizes. Any implementation choice still requires Main's measured full-path and physical-context validation.

next_three_research_scopes.title: Reusable command submission for a dynamic long-prefill graph
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: If current full-boundary attribution shows host command/copy submission is material outside waits, compare direct per-command submission with reusable SYCL/Level Zero command lists or graph-like replay for a chunked prefill DAG. Which approach lowers repeated host work while preserving dynamic pointers, event dependencies, cancellation, async-error reporting and safe resource retirement?
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use official SYCL, oneAPI and Level Zero references plus original non-LLM GPU command-replay or launch-overhead studies. Compare at least two replay mechanisms with ordinary submission, and include counterevidence for re-record/update overhead, unsupported dynamic arguments, queue ordering, portability and cases where device work or completion waiting dominates. Avoid repeating R751's wait-policy survey, R765's UR host-copy source audit or R769's transfer/compute overlap analysis.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1,200–1,700 words; at most 6 substantive primary sources, exact links and a capability/applicability matrix.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisites: A fresh, closed attribution after current source integration must show repeated command/copy submission is a material part of the active long-prefill critical path, separately from busy completion waits and host computation.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: The current index has prior v3 attribution with 25.793 CPU seconds in residual host-copy submission and 165.704 seconds in explicit waits, but no fresh post-integration full-boundary timing was supplied for R771. Do not dispatch on the historical CPU totals alone.
